Subject: Hyperion v1.2 handoff — proposed temporary version lock and telemetry gating

Team —

Orion has formally signaled readiness to onboard Hyperion v1.2 as their production serving model next month. They want us to pin v1.2 for the initial 4-week window post-ingestion to keep latency/quality stable while they exercise their internal canary traffic.

As part of that request, Product is proposing a temporary version lock (four weeks) with the following asks:
- Lock serving variant to hyperion:v1.2 for Orion's account (ORION-2027-1452) during the window.
- Enable verbose telemetry for the pinned variant (latency percentiles, token breakdown, prompt/response hash sampling).
- Staggered rollout plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 72 hours once integration passes staging.
- Pre-approved fallback to hyperion:v1.1 if tokenization or correctness regressions exceed thresholds in the telemetry checklist.

Questions for the group:
1) Marcus / Dev — any compatibility red flags (tokenizer, kv-cache layout, attention kernel mismatch) you need before we agree to the lock?
2) Grace — will this require a special routing rule or can we express the lock via the existing rollout config?
3) Priyom — can you scope the telemetry gating checks and provide a short checklist we can send to Orion?

I attached the initial compatibility report Orion supplied and a telemetry checklist draft. Please reply with blockers or sign-off by EOD 12/09 so I can confirm with Orion.

Thanks,

— Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Manager, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@orion.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hyperion v1.2 handoff — proposed temporary version lock and telemetry gating

Laura —

Thanks for the summary. Quick flag from infra: Hyperion's tokenizer config in their manifest differs from our canonical BPE mapping (map_v2 vs map_v1). That alone can cause off-by-one tokenization shifts which surface as short hallucinations on prompts that rely on exact offsets. Before we grant a lock I need one of the following:
- Orion publishes a tokenizer conversion map and we run a token-diff test on our staging harness; or
- We serve a conversion shim at ingress (adds ~3–5ms per request) and mark it in the rollout notes.

Also, their KV cache layout appears to use a different key serialization that will break cross-variant caching (we won't be able to transparently fall back between v1.1 and v1.2 without cache flushes). That means the fallback behavior will need an explicit plan to avoid user-visible latency spikes.

Suggested next steps:
- Dev, can you validate feasibility of an ingress token shim and estimate perf cost?
- Priyom, add a telemetry trigger to watch for a 2x increase in tail latency when fallback occurs.

I'm fine with a temporary pin once those two items are mitigated.

— Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Marcus / all —

Thanks for the callouts. Short answers and proposed mitigations:

1) Tokenizer mismatch — we can ship a tiny deterministic conversion layer at ingress that translates Orion tokens to our canonical BPE. It introduces an estimated 3.8ms median overhead (worst-case 9ms under load). We'll include this as an opt-in per-account shim so it only applies to ORION.

2) KV cache serialization — true, they use a different serialization which prevents cache reuse across v1.1 and v1.2. For the fallback plan I propose:
- When we detect a fallback event, we mark the request with a header and trigger an async background cache warmup for the fallback variant for that account.
- We will also set conservative SLOs on fallback traffic for the first 24 hours and enable a low-latency sampling feed for Serena (CS) to inspect user-visible regressions.

3) Staging window — we need a 48-hour dedicated staging window where Orion runs their test harness. I'll schedule a staging slot and create an automated token-diff job (INF-7291).

Action items assigned: 
- Dev: implement ingress conversion shim and token-diff job (ETA 5 business days).
- Marcus: validate perf impact for canary at 10% traffic and confirm KV warmup strategy (ETA 2 business days).
- Priyom: finalize telemetry checklist and thresholds — aim to share with Orion for sign-off.

I've linked the Jira ticket and the draft Drive handoff doc. I also attached the compatibility report we received. If we can close on these items by EOD 12/09 I will communicate a tentative 4-week lock window to Orion starting 01/05/2028.

— Dev Patel
Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Laura / team —

I put together a lean telemetry gating checklist and threshold proposals for the onboarding window. High-level items:
- Latency: 95th percentile increase > 20% relative to baseline => auto-alert and hold canary.
- Tokenization diffs: >0.5% of sampled prompts show token alignment breaks => require immediate rollback candidate evaluation.
- Correctness regression: >1.5% of sampled golden prompts deviate beyond acceptable BLEU-like threshold => hold and triage.
- Fallback latency spike: any instance of fallback that causes tail p50->p99 increase > 2x => escalate to infra.

I uploaded the checklist and a small telemetry dashboard template to the Drive link in the metadata. I've also added INF-7291 to watch token-diff output and will post nightly summaries during the 4-week window.

If everyone is good with the ingress shim and KV warmup plan, I sign off on the temporary lock.

— Priyom Das
Senior Reliability Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference
